liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (2 reviews): Twenty-three minutes with more melodic jamming than typical '72 versions; Rages after bass-driven opening; band jams hard for about two minutes [6][7]
- **Black Throated Wind** (1 review): Slower than normal and very unique; one of the best Berthas ever heard [9]
- Short but classic, intense, surging, and melodic jam; essential Dead performance [6]
- Described as blazing, aggressive, and a step further than most other jams [7]

## The recordings

- **gd72-04-21.fm.vernon.9380.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 7 songs; 78 min; rated 3.21/5 by 19 [1]. Said about its sound: Feedback during Loser was so severe the band stopped; Bobby yelled at the error; Sound quality sounds antique, like a real tape reel, adding to the quality; Tape suffered from drag over successive generations, slowing the original tempo [5][9][11]
- **gd1972-04-21.116404.sbd.berger.sndchk.flac16**: soundboard; 2 songs; 25 min [2]. Said about its sound: Wow and flutter problems present; pitch was way off; not in box set [2]

## Around the show

- Loser and Black Throated Wind likely from soundcheck; band stopped to fix feedback [12]
- Beat Club described as a disco joint managed by strict German staff [13]
- Live TV broadcast with no audience; Robert Hunter danced to energize the music [14]
- Europe '72 run had consistent quality; Pigpen's final shows make these extra special [8]
- Not recommended for newcomers; try Rotterdam May 11 and London May 26 instead [8]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-04-21.fm.vernon.9380.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: SBD to FM to MR to PCM to DAT to CDR; via Raoul Duke; Seeded to etree by Matt Vernon; includes soundcheck, missing three songs [1]
- **gd1972-04-21.116404.sbd.berger.sndchk.flac16**: transferred by Rob Berger; source: Source: SBD -> ? (Remaster of shinid 9380 soundcheck portion). [2]. Also: Listed as SBD to FM reel master to PCM to DAT to CDR; accuracy unknown [2]
